# Testing

Three levels, not one more. The right level is the cheapest one that genuinely exercises the behaviour.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Base rules

### Rules

- **CORE-020** · guidance — There are exactly three test levels, unit (no application), slice (`httpx.ASGITransport` with the service layer substituted) and integration (`httpx` with Testcontainers).
  Why: Each level has a cost and a purpose; a fourth category is where confusion starts.
- **CORE-021** · `pytest` — Persistence is tested against the real database engine through Testcontainers; SQLite is never substituted for it.
  Why: SQLite knows neither the column types, nor the deferred constraints, nor the SQL that Alembic generates.
- **CORE-022** · guidance — Test functions are named `test_<method>_<condition>_<expected_result>`, in snake_case.
  Why: A failing test name must say what broke without opening the file.
- **CORE-023** · `pytest` — Every test carries exactly one level marker, `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.slice` or `@pytest.mark.integration`.
  Why: `pytest -m "not integration"` must run the whole suite that needs no Docker.
- **CORE-024** · guidance — No numeric coverage threshold is imposed; a test is judged on what it verifies.
  Why: A percentage target produces assertion-free tests written to satisfy the metric.
- **CORE-025** · guidance — Every feature ships with at least one unit test, plus the slice test of each endpoint it adds.
  Why: The reference example shows one test per level; new code follows the same shape.

### Anti-patterns

- **CORE-AP-020** · guidance — Starting the whole application for every test because it "always works".
  Why: The suite becomes minutes long and nobody runs it before pushing.
  Instead: Pick the cheapest level that exercises the behaviour under test.
- **CORE-AP-021** · guidance — Pointing the test database URL at `sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:` to make the suite faster.
  Why: The test validates the fake, not the SQL that will run in production.
  Instead: An integration test on the Testcontainers database.
- **CORE-AP-022** · guidance — Test names such as `test_1`, `test_it_works` or `test_create`.
  Why: The name carries no information when it appears in a failure report.
  Instead: `test_create_title_blank_returns_400`: method, condition, expected result.
